title: Work view: fetch the full Work set automatically (pages of 200) and show closed work through the existing lifecycle filter
outcome: Fetch the full Work set through existing ls --all cursor, serial requested pages of 200 until end; append incrementally in bounded measured list preserving selection/scroll. Open is the default; completed, cancelled and superseded work is reachable through lifecycle filtering and existing Updated sort. Existing progress, changed-list reload, Retry and query-generation fences remain. Exact independent coordinator concurrence7f2636741e0540a99a5cb5a7f7dbeb10, Fable2#395, Greg relay Advisor#833. Each row also shows muted second-line last-updated metadata from the existing payload; independent concurrence6ae47bffe8df4efbb51ceae9609dec66, Fable2#399/Advisor#835.
acceptance: Opening the Work view fetches the full Work set (all lifecycles, through the existing Engram `ls --all` cursor) automatically and serially in pages of 200, following Engram's more/after until it reports the end, with no click or scroll required and exactly one request in flight; the full set is eventually loaded, including more than 1,000 items; tests show it.

Each page is appended or merged incrementally into a bounded (virtualized or equivalent) store without wholesale list replacement; scroll position and selection are preserved while pages arrive; with 1,200 loaded rows the number of rendered row elements stays bounded; tests show it.

Open work remains the default view, and closed work (completed, cancelled and superseded) is reachable through the existing lifecycle filtering path and ordered by the existing Updated sort; no new closed-specific API or separate closed-order surface is added; tests show closed rows reachable and sorted by Updated.

Compact progress and end-of-list states are visible; a cursor invalidated by a membership change stops and shows an explicit 'list changed; reload' state; a failed page shows Retry, which re-requests the same cursor once per activation with no automatic retry loop; a byte-bounded page reporting more with no cursor stops visibly instead of looping; tests show each.
Changing a filter or the search restarts from the first page and discards any in-flight continuation of the old query, so no stale page is appended; a test shows it.
`npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and the full five-stage gate passes on the exact landed input.

Each Work row shows its last-updated time from the existing updated_at field as muted metadata on its second line, beside or after the labels, in a compact locale-aware or relative form whose exact timestamp is available as an accessible title; no API is added, and pages arriving do not redraw existing rows wholesale; a test shows it.
